precepts.text: He returns to His place until they acknowledge their offense and seek His face, and in their affliction they will seek Him early.
precepts.point: The houses thrown down by the mount and the sword would be filled with the dead bodies of men He slew in His anger, for He hid His face from the city for all their wickedness.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
The Lord says of Jerusalem, “for all whose wickedness I have hid my face from this city.” Hosea tells how long he hides it: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

He returns to his place until they acknowledge their offense and seek his face. The houses thrown down and filled with the dead bodies of men slain in his anger and his fury are the affliction, and in their affliction they will seek him early. That is why he still tells Jeremiah in the prison, Call unto me, and I will answer thee.

precepts.text: We would have to acknowledge our offenses before the Most High, and in the affliction of the other nations we return to Him.
precepts.point: The houses thrown down by the mount and the sword would be filled with the dead bodies of men He slew in His anger, for He hid His face from the city for all their wickedness.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
Solomon prayed for the very affliction Jeremiah is watching come: “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness”.

We would have to acknowledge our offenses before the Most High. He hid his face from the city for all their wickedness, and it is in the land of them that carried us captive, in the affliction of the other nations, that we bethink ourselves, repent, and return to him. Then the one who hid his face answers when we call.

precepts.text: In that day He will raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, close up the breaches, and build it as in the days of old.
precepts.point: It shall be to Him a name of joy, a praise, and an honor before all nations, who will fear and tremble at the goodness He procures, for the nations know this is true and are struck when they see us carry ourselves as sons and daughters of the covenant.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
The Lord will cause the captivity of Judah and the captivity of Israel to return, “and will build them, as at the first.” Amos speaks of that building: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof; and I will raise up his ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old”.

In that day he raises up the fallen tabernacle of David, closes up the breaches, and builds it as in the days of old, which is building them as at the first. It has not yet been fulfilled; there is still much violence in Israel and against us, and the abundance of peace and truth is still to be revealed. When it is, it will be a name of joy, a praise and an honour before all the nations of the earth.

precepts.text: Even the New Testament points to future prophecy that He will return and build again the ruins of the tabernacle of David.
precepts.point: It shall be to Him a name of joy, a praise, and an honor before all nations, who will fear and tremble at the goodness He procures, for the nations know this is true and are struck when they see us carry ourselves as sons and daughters of the covenant.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
The New Testament reads the same prophecy as still ahead: “And to this agree the words of the prophets; as it is written, After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down; and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up”.

Even the New Testament points to future prophecy: he will return and build again the ruins of the tabernacle of David. That is the health and cure of Jeremiah 33, the captivity of Judah and Israel returned and built as at the first, cleansed from all their iniquity. The nations know this is true, and they are struck when they see us carry ourselves as sons and daughters of the covenant; they shall fear and tremble for all the goodness and prosperity he procures.

precepts.text: To the Israelites pertain the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the law, the service of God, and the promises, which is why we read the prophecy everywhere in the Old Testament.
precepts.point: Behold, the days come that He will perform the good thing He has promised to the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
“Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will perform that good thing which I have promised unto the house of Israel and to the house of Judah.” Paul tells who the promises belong to: “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises”.

To the Israelites pertain the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the law, the service of God, and the promises. That is why we read the prophecy everywhere in the Old Testament: the voice of joy and gladness heard again in the desolate cities, the flocks passing again under the hands of him that telleth them, the captivity of the land returned as at the first, are promises to the house of Israel and the house of Judah and no one else.

precepts.text: God has not cast away His people whom He foreknew, and we are the living proof, our hearts turned back to keeping the commandments and the faith of Christ without bodily eyes having seen Him.
precepts.point: He tells Jeremiah not to regard the people who say the two families the Most High chose He has now cast off and despised so they should be no more a nation; if His covenant with day and night stands, He will not cast away the seed of Jacob and David.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

precepts.why:
The people said the two families the Lord had chosen “he hath even cast them off”, that they should be no more a nation. The Lord answers that as surely as his covenant with day and night stands, he will not cast away the seed of Jacob and David. Paul asks the same question and gives the same answer: “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.”

God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew, and we are the living proof. Our hearts are turned back to keeping the commandments and the faith of Christ without our bodily eyes ever having seen him. The covenant with David that he should not want a son to reign upon his throne, and the seed of David and the Levites multiplied like the host of heaven and the sand of the sea, stand as sure as day and night in their season, for he will cause our captivity to return and have mercy on us.

precepts.text: The word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah while he was yet shut up in the court of the prison.
precepts.point: Every man of the Most High went to prison, from Jeremiah, John, and Christ himself to Paul and Silas, as every man who fought oppression was jailed; the teacher who pushes prophecy is counted the same threat.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Moreover the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah the second time, while he was yet shut up in the court of the prison”. The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in prison.

Every man of the Most High went to prison. Read the lives of the apostles and prophets as a pattern for today: the apostles put in the common prison here, Jeremiah shut up in the court of the prison before them. What the forefathers suffered will come again under America, the last kingdom, and worse.

points: The two families is Judah and Israel. He hath even cast them off: that was the thought; that's why it got a question mark there. Thus they have despised my people: because the doctrine started to come up even back then. God has destroyed the two kingdoms, God has destroyed the 12 tribes of Israel. This supersessionism, replacement theology.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: If my covenant be not with day and night: because day and night is still here, the ordinances of heaven and earth is still here. Then and only then will I cast away the seed of Jacob, and David my servant, so that I will not take any of his seed to be rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You know who comes out of that seed? Christ. So then there'd be no need for Christ. But there was a need; Christ did come, which means the 12 tribes are still here today.

For I will cause their captivity to return: meaning he's going to bring us back to the land out of this misery we in. The way it sounds like he's going to put us back in slavery; that's not what he's saying. Return where? To our homeland, and have mercy. He's just calling us the captivity, not that he's going to put us back in the captivity.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Considerest thou not what this people have spoken, saying, The two families which the Lord hath chosen, he hath even cast them off? The two families are Judah and Israel. Thus they have despised my people, that they should be no more a nation before them. Many Christian churches teach that the twelve tribes of Israel have been destroyed and God is dealing with the church now; when they say church, they are talking about Roman Catholics and Protestants.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: Thus saith the Lord; If my covenant be not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth; then will I cast away the seed of Jacob, and David my servant, so that I will not take any of his seed to be rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You know what that proves? We are going to be rulers, because the sun is still here, the moon is still here, and the stars are still here.
For I will cause their captivity to return, and have mercy on them. He is going to have mercy on us. Twelve tribes. And with that, shalom.
